sources.citation: Keesing, Roger M. 1985. Kwaio Grammar. Pacific Linguistics B-88. Canberra: ANU. (Internet Archive copy of sealang.net; the ANU handle 1885/146505 labelled 'Kwaio Grammar' actually serves Stokhof 1979 Woisika II — wrong file)
sources.note: Describes KWAIO (Sinalagu/'Xwaio' dialect), not Dori'o. §1.2.2 Stress, pp. 9-11: 'Stress within morphemes is, with few exceptions, placed on the penultimate vowel. Stress is somewhat heavier on the penultimate vowel of the final segment of a polymorphemic form.' Exceptions: CVV verb bases + monosyllabic object suffix do not shift stress; unanalysable trisyllables get roughly equal stress on the first two vowels; analysable trisyllables have penultimate primary + initial secondary stress. Intro pp. 3-4: 'Kwaio and two closely related dialects, Kwarekwareo (Doori'o) on the west coast and Kwaikw…

sources.note: 206 items in broad phonemic transcription (e.g. gagaʔu-na 'hand', ʔabu-na 'blood', mɔʔɔsu 'sleep'); no stress marks, no prosodic notes.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands Languages: An Internal Classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU. (Dori'o = wordlist 73 'Dori'o (Ma)', ~900 speakers)
sources.note: Nothing. The book gives a language list (ch. 4), POC consonant/vowel correspondence tables per list (ch. 6-7) and ~500-item wordlists; the only occurrences of 'stress' are prose ('It is stressed however..') and footnotes on reflexes 'in unstressed position'. No statement on stress placement for Dori'o or any other language.

sources.citation: Keesing, Roger M. 1975. Kwaio dictionary. Pacific Linguistics C-35. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Kwaio only. Intro p. ix: 'A Kwaioan subgroup including Kwaio and, on the north coast, Kwaikwaio, and, on the south coast, Kwarekwareo (or Doore'o). The latter two dialects.. manifest most of the sound shifts in the direction of 'Are'are'; Keesing used a Kwarekwareo informant in 1970 but gives no Dori'o phonology. Vowel table p. xv notes /e/ = [e:] unstressed, [e] stressed (Kwaio); no placement rule.
